title: SKU consolidation and stagger plan for regional staging
content:
Purpose:
This is a working plan for consolidating our GPU SKU mix and staggering procurement orders across vendors/regions to reduce lead-time variability, lower hold costs, and make regional staging more predictable for the next 18 months of growth. Focus is on practical heuristics we can push to procurement and SRE for immediate action.

Summary of the ask:
- Reduce active SKU count across core fleets to 3 families for primary production lanes: H100-80GB, A100-80GB, and L40S.
- Create a 3-tier regional staging network (primary hub, secondary hub, overflow pool) to absorb shipment variance.
- Stagger orders across vendor windows and introduce an alternating 6/4 cadence per SKU to avoid simultaneous long-lead deliveries.

Key assumptions (please validate):
- Average burn rate (prod + canary) = 1.9 PFLOPs/month equivalent across NA + EU.
- Target utilization for production pools = 78% (buffered by caching/batching).
- Spot/lease fallback capacity can cover up to 12% of bursts for <72 hours.
- Vendor lead times (typical): H100 (90–140 days), A100 (40–80 days), L40S (30–65 days) — see table below.

Proposed SKU mix by role (percent of new inbound capacity):
- H100-80GB (inference heavy / high throughput): 45%
- A100-80GB (balanced training+inference): 35%
- L40S (cost-efficient inference & embedding): 20%

Staggering cadence (order windows):
- Month A: H100 tranche (60% of monthly H100 need) + small A100 buffer (20%).
- Month B: A100 tranche (80% of monthly A100 need).
- Month C: L40S tranche (100% of monthly L40S need) + spot lease renewals.
- Repeat cadence, with periodic micro-orders in between for critical capacity.

Regional staging targets (goal: 6–10 week runway at primary hub):
- NA-primary (us-west-2 + us-east-1 combined): 6–10 weeks of consumption (preferred for H100-heavy workloads)
- EU-primary (eu-west-1): 6 weeks baseline, scale to 8–10 weeks in Q2 if demand grows
- APAC overflow (asia-south1 staging): 4–6 weeks, use ephemeral leasing for >2 week bursts

Lead-time and vendor reliability table (working estimates):
- VendorX (direct OEM partner): H100 - median 110 days (std dev 20), A100 - median 50 days (std dev 12)
- ChannelY (authorized reseller): H100 - median 95 days (std dev 35), A100 - median 60 days (std dev 18), L40S - median 40 days (std dev 10)
- BrokerZ (refurb/lease broker): L40S - median 20 days (std dev 8), short-term leases 2–14 days

Reorder policy (practical heuristic):
- Reorder point R = (lead_time_days * avg_daily_burn) + safety_buffer_days * avg_daily_burn.
- Safety buffer by SKU: H100 = 35 days, A100 = 18 days, L40S = 12 days (higher for H100 due to variance).
- Default order quantity = next two cadence tranches (gives batching discount) unless inventory age > 9 months.

Scenario planning (three quick scenarios):
1) Normal growth (+8% month): Maintain cadence, increase NA-primary staging by one tranche per quarter.
2) Sudden demand surge (+40% quarter): Trigger emergency short-term lease window and flip to H100 priority; pull A100 into secondary backlog.
3) Vendor delay (H100 slips +60 days): Pull from channel inventory (if available), accelerate A100 to cover compute for mixed workloads, and open expedited freight for top-priority customer buckets.

Operational runbook (how teams act):
- Procurement: place cadence orders into vendor pipelines 14 days before tranche start, confirm ship windows with vendor rep; escalate to supplier_ops@redwood if median lead > 120 days.
- SRE/Capacity: maintain staging counts on daily dashboard (alert at <8 weeks NA-primary runway).
- Finance: track committed spend vs expected burn monthly; flag >10% variance to FP&A.

Open questions / blockers:
- Do we have legal SLAs that allow penalty-free staggered deliveries across multiple vendors? (Proc/legal)
- Confirm permissibility of relocating unopened racks between staging hubs (Ops/compliance)
- Validate freight insurance costs for expedited lanes (Finance/logistics)

Quick spreadsheet snapshot (paste into sheet for modeling):
Headers: month, region, sku, qty_ordered, est_arrival_days, onboard_date, notes
Example rows:
2026-02, NA-primary, H100-80GB, 40, 110, 2026-05-01, tranche-A
2026-03, EU-primary, A100-80GB, 60, 55, 2026-04-25, tranche-B
2026-04, APAC, L40S, 30, 35, 2026-05-10, overflow+leases

Short-term action items (next 30 days):
- [Procurement] Lock tranche windows and send preliminary POs to VendorX and ChannelY (owner: Evan).
- [SRE] Add NA-primary runway gauge to capacity dashboard with 7-day moving avg consumption (owner: Maya).
- [Finance] Get expedited freight cost estimate for H100 partial shipments (owner: Lucas).
- [Legal] Quick review on multi-vendor SLA interaction (owner: Sofia).

Notes to self / context fragments:
- Consolidation tradeoff: fewer SKUs lowers variance and simplifies kernel tuning but increases exposure if a vendor channel fails for that SKU. Keep contingency lane (refurb/lease) for worst-case.
- Consider a small dedicated queue of hybrid A100/H100 nodes for training that can be re-labeled to inference if needed (costly but gives flexibility).

Decision log (running):
- 2025-11-07: Draft plan created (S. Martinez)
- 2025-11-21: Procurement agreed to attempt 6/4 cadence pilot in NA for Q1 2026 (E. Liu)
